newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Gasoline stocks in APIs seen up on output.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Gasoline stocks in APIs seen up on output.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.

Despite healthy gasoline demand, gasoline stocks are expected by traders to show a moderate gain of about one to two million barrels in Tuesday evening's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
"High domestic production coupled with fairly high imports with hardly any refinery snags to speak of should outdo high demand," said Prudential Securities analyst Richard Redash.
Traders expected gasoline output to continue at around eight million barrels a day while imports are running near 500,000 barrels a day.
Meanwhile, analysts expect implied gasoline demand to peak at a little more than eight million barrels a day as the summer begins, a level below the supply coming in.
"I expect gasoline demand to peak in the next several weeks, but I doubt we will have record demand this year," said Bill O'Grady, analyst with A.G. Edwards.
To be sure, current gasoline production only reflects seasonal consumption which is strongest in the summer.

The high gasoline output has resulted in a torrid refinery run rate that stood at 98.3 percent for the week ended Jun 6 and which analysts suppose remained steady to only slightly off for the week ended June 13, the period covered by Tuesday night's data.
"Crude stocks are supposed to be down due to the exceptionally high run rate," said O'Grady.
Crude stocks are seen off two to three million barrels, but analysts noted total crude inventories will remain at a comfortable surplus to a year ago.

Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, are expected to rise two to three million barrels. Although distillate production is healthy due to the runup in refinery utilization capacity, heating oil use is out of season.
